title: Vue
description: The native Vue 3 components of minerva-design/vue: installation, the global stylesheet, per-component imports or the plugin, v-model and emits, theming with nested ConfigProvider scopes, Nuxt / SSR and Volar typings.

install.title: Installation
install.text: Install the package with Vue 3.5 or later (an optional peer dependency). minerva-design/vue ships ES modules and type declarations; the components are Vue single-file components built on the same headless core as React.
install.stylesheet: Import the global stylesheet once, in your entry file. It is the same file as for React: the Vue components render the same class names and styling hooks, so design tokens, themes, palettes and CSS variables apply unchanged.

usage.title: Using the components
usage.text: Import components by name; your bundler keeps only those you use (every export is side-effect free).
usage.vModel: Values are v-model (modelValue / update:modelValue) with defaultValue / defaultChecked for uncontrolled use; overlays use v-model:open (defaultOpen), other controlled props v-model:name (v-model:current, v-model:expanded).
usage.events: Events are typed emits named like the React callbacks without "on": onChange → @change, onOpenChange → @open-change, with the same arguments.
usage.slots: Rich content goes in slots (#trigger, #title, #start-icon...); simple texts stay props (title, description, label).

plugin.title: Global registration
plugin.text: Prefer named imports. To use the components in every template without importing them, install the plugin: it registers them as <MnButton>, <MnModal>... (the prefix is configurable).
plugin.types: The global components are typed for Vue - Official (Volar) and vue-tsc by the minerva-design/vue/global typings:

charts.title: Charts
charts.text: MinervaVue does not register the charts, so that apps without charts never load the chart engine. Import the charts by name from minerva-design/vue/charts (recommended; they are also still exported by minerva-design/vue), or install the opt-in MinervaVueCharts plugin of minerva-design/vue/charts: it registers <MnLineChart>, <MnPieChart>, <MnTradingChart>... with the same prefix option, typed by minerva-design/vue/charts-global.

migration.title: Upgrading from 1.4
migration.text: Since 1.5, app.use(MinervaVue) no longer registers <MnChart>, <MnLineChart> and the other chart components. If your templates use them without importing them, add app.use(MinervaVueCharts) from minerva-design/vue/charts (with the same prefix as MinervaVue, if you changed it) and add minerva-design/vue/charts-global to the types of tsconfig.json. Named imports are unchanged.

dev.title: Charts and the Vite dev server
dev.text: Production builds tree-shake the charts: an app that never imports a chart ships no chart code, with or without app.use(MinervaVue). In development, however, Vite pre-bundles every export of minerva-design/vue into a single file, so the chart wrappers and the chart engine (about 0.7 MB unminified) are part of it even when no chart is used. The pre-bundle is cached in node_modules/.vite, so this only costs parsing time on a full page load. If your app uses charts, import them from minerva-design/vue/charts and list both entries in optimizeDeps.include, so that Vite pre-bundles them together at startup instead of re-optimizing and reloading the page the first time a chart is imported:
dev.exclude: Excluding minerva-design/charts/core from optimizeDeps does not help: the Vue components reach the engine through a relative path inside the package. Excluding minerva-design/vue does not help either: the browser would then load hundreds of unbundled modules, the charts included.
dev.future: minerva-design/vue keeps exporting the chart components until the next major version, because removing them would break existing named imports. In 2.0 they will only be exported by minerva-design/vue/charts, which will also remove them from the dev pre-bundle. Importing charts from minerva-design/vue/charts today makes that upgrade a no-op.

theming.title: Theming and i18n
theming.text: ConfigProvider sets the theme, palette, design axes and the language of the built-in texts. The root provider owns <html>; a nested provider scopes its overrides to its subtree, overlays included (they are teleported into a matching scope container).

nuxt.title: Nuxt and server rendering
nuxt.text: The components render on the server with vue/server-renderer and hydrate without mismatches: overlays (modals, popovers, toasts) mount on the client, ids come from Vue's useId(), and nothing touches the DOM during setup. In Nuxt, add the stylesheet to css and, optionally, a plugin for the global components (and MinervaVueCharts for the global charts).

islands.title: Vue islands
islands.text: Mounting a Vue app inside a page whose theme is owned by another framework (micro-frontends, a Vue widget in a React page)? Call provideEmbeddedScope before mounting: its providers then behave as nested ones and never write <html>. This documentation uses it for every Vue demo.

snippets.source:
pnpm add minerva-design vue
# or: npm install minerva-design vue

<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from "vue";
// named imports: only what you use ends up in the bundle
import { Button, Input, Modal, Switch } from "minerva-design/vue";

const name = ref("");
const notify = ref(true);
const open = ref(false);
</script>

<template>
  <Input v-model="name" placeholder="Name" />
  <Switch v-model="notify" label="Email notifications" />
  <Button :disabled="!name" @click="open = true">Save</Button>

  <Modal v-model:open="open" title="Saved" description="Your profile is up to date.">
    <Button @click="open = false">Close</Button>
  </Modal>
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { ConfigProvider, ThemeToggle, useTheme } from "minerva-design/vue";
</script>

<template>
  <!-- root provider: owns <html> (theme, palette, design) and the language -->
  <ConfigProvider theme="system" palette="ocean" :locale="{ language: 'fr' }" persist>
    <ThemeToggle />
    <RouterView />

    <!-- nested provider: scoped to its subtree (and its overlays) -->
    <ConfigProvider theme="dark" density="compact">
      <AdminPanel />
    </ConfigProvider>
  </ConfigProvider>
</template>
